name: Supplement Safety & Interaction Guardrails
purpose: Keep genotype-informed supplement prompts food-first, lab-aware, medication-aware, and bounded by nutrient safety limits.
principles: A genotype can suggest a question; it cannot establish that a person needs a supplement.
Prefer food and measured deficiency/excess context before supplements when medically appropriate.
Review medications, pregnancy/lactation, kidney/liver disease, allergies, and total intake before starting a supplement.
Do not stack multiple products containing the same nutrient without checking the total amount and upper limits.

rules.label: Selenium / Brazil-nut safety
food_first: Prefer ordinary food sources and measured clinical context over a genotype-driven selenium supplement.
avoid: Do not combine Brazil nuts, multivitamins, thyroid products, and selenium supplements without totaling selenium intake.
Do not use GPX1 genotype alone to justify selenium supplementation.
confirm_with: thyroid, kidney, pregnancy/lactation, and clinical context
selenium testing only when clinically indicated

rules.label: Magnesium food and interaction safety
food_first: Favor magnesium-rich foods before a supplement when they fit the user's diet and medical needs.
avoid: Do not exceed the adult upper limit for magnesium from supplements and medicines without clinician guidance.
Do not use supplemental magnesium casually with kidney disease or without reviewing antibiotic, bisphosphonate, diuretic, and acid-suppressing medication context.
confirm_with: symptoms or labs when deficiency is suspected

rules.label: Omega-3 food versus supplement safety
food_first: Prefer appropriate fish or algal food sources when compatible with allergy, pregnancy, mercury, and dietary constraints.
avoid: Do not treat a FADS genotype as proof that a high-dose omega-3 supplement is needed.
Do not start high-dose omega-3 supplements without reviewing anticoagulants, bleeding risk, cardiovascular history, and other medicines.

rules.label: Iron supplementation requires evidence
food_first: Use allowed iron-containing foods while confirming whether the problem is deficiency, excess, blood loss, or another cause.
avoid: Do not start iron supplements from fatigue, HFE genotype, or a single SNP without iron studies and clinical context.
Do not take iron alongside interacting medicines without pharmacist guidance.
confirm_with: CBC, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and clinician interpretation
bleeding, gastrointestinal, kidney, pregnancy, and medication context

rules.label: Vitamin D dose and lab safety
food_first: Use measured 25(OH)D and clinical context to guide vitamin D decisions rather than a receptor SNP alone.
avoid: Do not use VDR, GC, DHCR7, or CYP2R1 genotype alone to justify megadose vitamin D.
Do not ignore calcium, kidney, parathyroid, pregnancy, or medication context.
confirm_with: calcium and kidney context when clinically indicated

rules.label: Folate and MTHFR guardrail
food_first: Favor folate-rich foods and clinically appropriate fortified foods; do not create a permanent folic-acid avoidance rule from MTHFR.
avoid: Do not avoid folic acid or switch to high-dose methylfolate solely because of an MTHFR SNP.
Do not use high-dose folate without checking B12, medications, pregnancy, and clinician guidance.
confirm_with: folate, B12, CBC/MCV, and homocysteine when clinically relevant

rules.label: Creatine and kidney-context safety
food_first: Treat creatine as a goal- and training-context option, not a genetic requirement.
avoid: Do not use genotype to prescribe a creatine dose or override kidney disease, abnormal kidney tests, pregnancy, or clinician restrictions.
confirm_with: training goal, hydration, kidney function, and current medications

do_not_do: Do not infer supplement need, safety, dose, or efficacy from a common SNP alone.
Do not treat supplement ideas as medication substitutes or use them to counteract a prescribed treatment.
Do not recommend a supplement while ignoring a user's allergy, eating-disorder risk, kidney/liver disease, pregnancy/lactation, or medication list.
